rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥāddah means conflict and enmity, the opposite of muwādah; their juxtaposition in 58:22 clarifies the sense.
rows.anchor: means “conflict and enmity.” It is the opposite of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contrasts people who turn to God and the Prophet only in hardship with professed believers who oppose them.
rows.anchor: In the previous paragraph, as is evident, the character of those people has been described who come only to God and His Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their clandestine propaganda targets Islamic directives they see as against their interests and aims to shake sincere Muslims’ faith.
rows.anchor: They would start a whispering campaign and clandestine propaganda against any directive of Islam which they felt was against their benefit and interest.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sympathies lay with Islam’s enemies, especially the Jews; Islahi identifies them as Jewish agents among the Muslims.
rows.anchor: They were the agents of the Jews among the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He points back to the turmoil in the affairs of ʿĀʾishah and Zaynab, discussed earlier in Sūrah al-Nūr and Sūrah al-Aḥzāb.
rows.anchor: Details of the turmoil they caused in the matters of ‘Ā’ishah (rta) and Zaynab (rta) have already been mentioned in S ūrah al-Nūr and S ūrah al-Aḥzāb.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In jāhiliyyah, ẓihār meant permanent divorce between husband and wife.
rows.anchor: In the age of jāhiliyyah, as referred to before, ẓihār signified a permanent divorce between a husband and wife.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opponents could misrepresent the Qur’anic concession on ẓihār as allowing marriage to mothers, sowing misconceptions; their mischief therefore had to be exposed.
rows.anchor: These miscreants could have easily begun the whispering campaign that Islam had, God forbid, allowed its followers to contract marriage with their mothers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear arguments refer to Qur’anic historical examples showing that those who oppose God’s prophets are ultimately humbled.
rows.anchor: to show that those who oppose God’s prophets are ultimately humbled.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers meant are active opponents of the Prophet; since their character matches earlier opponents, the same divine law brings them humiliation.
rows.anchor: The reference is to those disbelievers who were proactive in opposing the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning came to pass when Quraysh were humbled and the Jews met their fate; hypocrites plotting under Jewish patronage shared that fate, detailed in following sūrahs.
rows.anchor: the power of the Quraysh was also humbled, and the Jews too met their fate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment was humiliating because it included execution, exile, and slavery, with no sympathy for them and universal condemnation.
rows.anchor: The punishment they were given has been called humiliating because they had to encounter punishments of execution, exile and slavery

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative yawm could attach to the previous verse’s punishment, but he prefers an omitted verb under standard Arabic principles.
rows.anchor: however, in my opinion, it is because of a suppressed verb as per common linguistic principles of Arabic

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly punishment is only a prelude; they must remember the day God resurrects them and brings their actions before them.
rows.anchor: they should also remember the day when the Almighty will raise them to life again

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamiʿan indicates that all elements and motives of the conspiracies will be assembled and each person shown who proposed or followed what.
rows.anchor: points to the fact that all the components and motives of the conspiracies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s informing them of their deeds entails their consequences, so they will face what they did.
rows.anchor: The Almighty will inform them of all their deeds so that they face their consequences.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human forgetfulness does not mean God has forgotten: He recorded every deed and fixed a day for the reward and punishment of each person.
rows.anchor: are meant to dispel a great misconception: people should not think that if they have forgotten everything they had done

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing declaration that God witnesses all things substantiates the assurance that He has not forgotten their deeds.
rows.anchor: substantiate what is just said: The Almighty is not

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is absent from nowhere; everything that happens in heaven and earth occurs before Him, and He is omnipresent.
rows.anchor: whatever happens in the heavens and the earth happens before Him and He is omnipresent.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 7 further explains God’s all-encompassing knowledge: He will present each person with all their deeds.
rows.anchor: This is a further explanation of the fact that each and everything in the heavens and the earth is in the knowledge of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general address in alam tara presents God’s knowledge as something evident to everyone.
rows.anchor: this style refers to the fact that this is something which should be evident to everyone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God created and governs the heavens and earth, and all things depend on His permission, He cannot be unaware of anything; Islahi links this reasoning to 67:14.
rows.anchor: when God is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and when He alone is running all their affairs

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those conspiring against God and the Prophet must remember that God accompanies private conversations, whether three converse or five, and likewise with fewer or more.
rows.anchor: when three of them are conversing in private, the fourth is God, and when five of them are conversing in private, the sixth is God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wherever clause means God is with them wherever they whisper, leaving no place in heaven or earth where they can hide.
rows.anchor: wherever they converse in secret, God will be with them. They cannot find any place in the heavens and the earth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They persist in the clandestine conversations they were forbidden to hold and brazenly discuss sin, transgression, and disobedience without shame or fear of God.
rows.anchor: They are neither ashamed on this nor have any fear of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apparently tried to stop their whispering at first, but they persisted and intensified their mischief, prompting these verses as a final warning.
rows.anchor: the Almighty tried to stop them; however, they never desisted; in fact, their mischief only increased.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their private talks contain no good because their hearts lack goodness, although secret conversation can concern good matters as the following verses indicate.
rows.anchor: there is nothing good in their private conversation, even though such conversation can relate to good things, as is mentioned in the succeeding verses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithm refers to sins where usurpation of rights is dominant.
rows.anchor: refers to sins in which the element of usurping rights is dominant

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUdwān refers to sins where transgression, rebellion, and arrogance are dominant.
rows.anchor: refers to sins in which the element of transgression, rebellion and arrogance is dominant.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together, ithm and ʿudwān encompass every kind of sin.
rows.anchor: When used together, these words embrace all types of sins.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The campaigns’ real objective is to incite Muslims to rebel against the Prophet and fracture their community.
rows.anchor: They want to incite Muslims to rebel against the Prophet (sws) in order to dismember their lot.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews nurtured and guided the hypocrites, whose aim was to sow mischief among the Companions before they became an impregnable force.
rows.anchor: These hypocrites, as has been indicated earlier, were nurtured and guided by the Jews.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God humiliated these plotters, while the community trained and organized by the Prophet humbled the enemies of truth.
rows.anchor: the faction of God which was organized by the training and education of the Prophet Muḥammad (sws) humbled all the enemies of the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deliberately reversed the prescribed greeting, saying death to the Prophet instead of peace, while God and the angels send him blessings.
rows.anchor: they pay salutations to him in exactly the opposite words prescribed by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wish for the Prophet’s death displays their callousness toward the person whom God and the angels bless.
rows.anchor: what doubt remains of their wretchedness who pray for death of the holy person on whom the Almighty and the angels send peace and blessings?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reassures the Prophet that God’s mercy and the angels’ blessings outweigh enemies’ wishes for his death, so he should not care about their prayers.
rows.anchor: so he should not care about what prayers these people make.
